clf-med-061.text: An in-memory database cache cluster needs EC2 instances with a very large amount of RAM relative to CPU because an entire 500 GB dataset must remain in memory for low-latency queries. Which EC2 instance-family category is designed for this profile?
clf-med-061.explanation: Memory Optimized instance families such as the R family provide a high amount of memory relative to vCPU and are well suited to large in-memory databases, caches, and real-time analytics workloads.
clf-med-061.hint: The critical resource is abundant RAM. Think of the EC2 family category specialized for memory-intensive workloads.
optionRationales: Memory Optimized instance families such as the R family provide a high amount of memory relative to vCPU and are well suited to large in-memory databases, caches, and real-time analytics workloads.
Compute Optimized C-family instances emphasize CPU capacity and provide a less memory-heavy profile than a workload keeping hundreds of gigabytes resident in RAM requires.
General Purpose M-family instances balance CPU and memory for broad workloads; a workload dominated by massive RAM requirements benefits from a memory-optimized family.
P-family instances emphasize accelerated computing with GPUs and are not selected primarily for a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio for database caches.

clf-med-062.text: An analytics platform stores data in Amazon S3 with a completely unpredictable access pattern: some objects are accessed daily for months, while others remain untouched for long periods and later become active again. The team wants storage costs optimized automatically without manual tier selection and without changing application performance for active data. Which S3 storage class is most appropriate?
options: S3 Standard with periodic manual deletion
clf-med-062.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors object access patterns and automatically moves objects among appropriate access tiers, making it well suited to data with unknown or changing access patterns.
clf-med-062.hint: The key word is unpredictable. Which S3 storage class automatically adjusts tiers based on observed access patterns?
optionRationales: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors object access patterns and automatically moves objects among appropriate access tiers, making it well suited to data with unknown or changing access patterns.
S3 Standard-IA is appropriate when infrequent access is known in advance and can be less efficient for objects that suddenly become active again.
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is intended for archival use and has retrieval characteristics that are not appropriate for data that may need immediate active access unpredictably.
Keeping all objects permanently in S3 Standard does not automatically optimize storage cost for long-unused data, and deleting data does not satisfy a requirement to keep it available.

clf-med-063.text: A processing pipeline produces intermediate files that are rarely accessed and can be regenerated easily from source data if they are lost. The team wants a lower-cost S3 option for infrequent access and is willing to give up resilience to the loss of an entire Availability Zone. Which storage class fits this case?
options: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)
clf-med-063.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone and costs less than multi-AZ infrequent-access storage, making it appropriate for infrequently accessed data that can be recreated if the Availability Zone is lost.
clf-med-063.hint: Re-creatable data does not require multi-zone resilience. Which infrequent-access storage class deliberately uses only one Availability Zone?
optionRationales: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone and costs less than multi-AZ infrequent-access storage, making it appropriate for infrequently accessed data that can be recreated if the Availability Zone is lost.
S3 Standard-IA stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones and therefore provides more resilience than the scenario requires.
S3 Standard is designed for frequently accessed data and costs more than an infrequent-access option for these rarely used intermediate files.

S3 Glacier Deep Archive is designed for long-term archival with much slower retrieval characteristics, which is not appropriate when intermediate files must remain immediately accessible when requested.

clf-med-064.text: An analyst accidentally deletes a critical object from an S3 bucket and causes hours of rework. The team wants Amazon S3 to preserve historical variants of each object so previous versions can be restored after accidental overwrite or deletion. Which S3 feature should be enabled?
clf-med-064.explanation: S3 Versioning preserves multiple versions of an object. Deleting a versioned object normally creates a delete marker, allowing previous versions to remain recoverable.
clf-med-064.hint: Think of the feature that turns each object change into a recoverable version rather than permanently replacing the previous copy.
optionRationales: S3 Versioning preserves multiple versions of an object. Deleting a versioned object normally creates a delete marker, allowing previous versions to remain recoverable.
S3 Transfer Acceleration improves long-distance transfer performance and does not preserve historical object versions.
S3 Lifecycle rules automate transitions and expirations for cost management and are not the primary accidental-overwrite recovery feature.
S3 Event Notifications inform other services about object events but do not restore or preserve deleted object content by themselves.

clf-med-065.text: Two teams in the same company use separate AWS VPCs, one for a financial system and one for a data lake, and need applications to communicate using private IP addresses without traffic traversing the public internet. Which AWS networking feature creates a direct private connection between the two VPCs?
options: An Internet Gateway in each VPC
clf-med-065.explanation: VPC Peering creates private network connectivity between two VPCs so resources can communicate using private IP addresses without routing through the public internet.
clf-med-065.hint: Think of the native peering capability that allows two VPCs to communicate directly through private addressing.
optionRationales: VPC Peering creates private network connectivity between two VPCs so resources can communicate using private IP addresses without routing through the public internet.
Internet Gateways provide public internet connectivity and do not create the private VPC-to-VPC path required here.
AWS Direct Connect links an on-premises network to AWS through dedicated connectivity; it is not primarily the mechanism for directly connecting two VPCs.
Route 53 Resolver provides DNS resolution capabilities and does not itself create the network path between VPCs.
